issues.evidence: The customer email is headed 'Customer email received on 2026-10-11' and Claire Martin writes 'I was too busy with work to report it earlier, sorry for the delay' — the claim was reported on 2026-10-11, 9 calendar days after the 2026-10-02 incident. Contract Article 4.1 (contract.pdf, 2630#10414, p.2) requires reporting within 5 days of the incident, and Article 7.1 (p.3) requires that a claim reported after the Article 4.1 deadline be referred to a Veridia claims handler who takes the decision ('A late claim is never refused automatically'). The staged result instead treats this as an in-deadline claim pending approval with payout €350, so the late-reporting fact and the mandatory handler referral are both wrong/missing.

verdict.summary: All other recorded facts match the email and contract (C2 collision is in the Policy Schedule, incident 2026-10-02, €650 quote, policyholder at fault, no third party, photos and repair quote received, no exclusion, no assessor needed under €1,500, €300 deductible since she is at fault and licensed since 2012), but the claim was actually reported on 2026-10-11, 9 days after the incident — beyond the 5-day deadline of Article 4.1 — so per Article 7.1 it must be referred to a claims handler for the decision rather than approved as staged.
